I enjoy political philosophy and will soon have a lot of time to read so what are your recommendations? For others as well as myself indicate the level of background knowledge necessary.
What are some books that expanded your ideals and knowledge or influenced your political ideologies

The History of Western Philosophy by Bertrand Russell. It's a beginner philosophy text and absolutely wonderful. Though my knowledge has expanded, I still re-read it every year. I first read it when I was fifteen, promptly drop out of high school, and never looked back. I can't say my finances have been better for it, but my quality of life sure has. To elaborate, it's not necessarily a book that leads you to a profound moment, but it does force you to re-evaluate life. You read through the history and general theories of life as they have progressed over time, and you, if you are a sane, rational person, necessarily have to ask questions about life that you have always taken as given but aren't necessarily so.

I would suggest it. Take, "Catcher in the Rye," and shove it. I would love to see, "The History of Western Philosophy," be cannon in high school.

Helllo y'all! I would like to introduce myself as a new member of the mod team!

I want to start off asking if there are any thing that you (35 people at the moment) want or believe we need to work on? Voat is still a site in progress so sadly there are some things that aren't available like in reddit (such as a wiki option which is great for helping categorize stuff and have information in one place). One thing I would like to possibly start is the Album of the Week that exists over /r/trance. Now it doesn't have to be a weekly thing, it can be bi-weekly, monthly, etc. While this sub is small, there's still plenty that we can do together.

I don't have any ideas beyond the obvious (keep posting tunes I like and that I think others will too). However, I've spotted one quirk of Voat (or maybe this subverse in particular) that seems interesting: it doesn't show new content very clearly. The first thing I do these days is click 'New' rather than 'Hot' and I wonder if people are missing out on new submissions if they don't.

For example, one of the tunes submitted recently was Life Less Ordinary (a great tune). However, it showed up on page three in the 'Hot' view, behind stuff that was submitted a few weeks ago! (As an aside, I've upvoted it now and probably ruined my point but you get the idea.) I also submitted three things today - but you'd have no idea if you didn't click 'New'!

I agree that the 'Hot' section could use some work to show more recent postings, especially at this point in time when we're trying to get more subscribers and the like.

A side note, the sidebar still calls this place a Whoaverse :P
